text:
Lynn Conway was born in Mount Vernon, New York, on January 2, 1938. She pursued higher education, earning B.S. and M.S.E.E. degrees from Columbia University's School of Engineering and Applied Science in 1962 and 1963, after having initially attempted a gender transition at MIT which led to her withdrawal in 1959.
Conway's career involved significant contributions to computer architecture and chip design. Working at IBM Research in 1964, she was part of the team designing the Advanced Computing Systems (ACS) project, where she invented multiple-issue out-of-order dynamic instruction scheduling. After transitioning and adopting a new identity, she joined Xerox PARC in 1973, where she founded the multiproject wafers (MPW) technology. Collaborating with Ivan Sutherland and Carver Mead, she co-authored *Introduction to VLSI Systems* , and her work on dimensionless, scalable design rules and the Metal Oxide Semiconductor Implementation Service (MOSIS) system was crucial to the Mead–Conway VLSI design methodology. She later joined DARPA in 1983 and became a professor at the University of Michigan in 1985, specializing in visual communications and control systems, and retired there in 1998.
